runs.note: weight load slow because no prefetch flag
the headline result — full stack on fresh node

key_findings: EBS snapshot of compile cache restores cleanly to a brand-new node — full AOT HIT delivered (8 ranks confirmed in logs)
Snapshot restore + attach + mount overhead: ~25 s total (volume create 9s + attach 10s + mount <1s)
AOT HIT delivers identical compile speedup on fresh node as on same-node (hostPath): 386 s vs 384 s
Cache survives node termination, instance store loss, AZ reboot — anything except snapshot deletion
Multi-variant capability validated: vLLM auto-picks correct hash dir; cache key is portable across nodes
Fast Snapshot Restore not needed for 500 MB cache — lazy load is fast enough
Operational implication: bake compile cache to EBS snapshot once per (vLLM_version × model × config), reuse forever until any of those change

production_recipe.step_1: Run a baker pod once per variant: cold start, write to EBS-mounted /root/.cache/vllm
production_recipe.step_2: After ready, snapshot the volume: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id $V
production_recipe.step_3: Tag snapshot with (model, vllm_version, tp_size, cudagraph_config) for retrieval
production_recipe.step_4: Production pods: PVC restored from snapshot, mounted at /root/.cache/vllm, AOT HIT every cold start
production_recipe.step_5: On vLLM upgrade or model swap: rebuild snapshot once, all replicas inherit

image_baked_cache.loss: image rebuild per variant; +500 MB image bloat
image_baked_cache.verdict: OK for fixed-config production, painful for experimentation

hostpath_cache_same_node.loss: lost on node termination, doesn't help fresh node

ebs_snapshot_cache.win: persistent across nodes, cheap (~$30/mo idle), multi-variant on one volume
